highlights:
## New Zealand’s Predicted Starting XI
[...]
Wood missed much of the 2025–26 Premier League season because of a knee injury that required surgery, and sat out the most recent international games in March. The veteran striker and national team legend is closing on 50 goals scored for his country. But the question of who can support his output, especially if at the age of 34 he’s struggling physically, remains.
[...]
Typical starters Sarpreet Singh, Matthew Garbett and Liberato Cacace have also been injured in 2026. The likes of Ben Old and Jesse Randall, left back Francis de Vries and 36-year-old frontman Kosta Barbarouses will step in to provide the creativity accordingly.

Clear underdogs facing a group-stage exit — but a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic dream, and recapturing 2010’s unbeaten magic the fairy-tale ceiling.
[...]
New Zealand are the clear underdogs of Group G and will struggle against Belgium, Egypt, and Iran on paper. The most likely outcome is a group-stage exit. But the All Whites’ organization and Chris Wood’s quality make them dangerous in a one-off match, and the expanded format means a single famous result could keep their hopes flickering. A first-ever World Cup win — perhaps against Egypt or Iran — is the realistic dream. Recapturing the unbeaten spirit of 2010 would be the fairy-tale ceiling.

### What to Expect / Prediction
[...]
Without a doubt, Uzbekistan are one of the underdogs in Group K, but they could make it to the next round via the best third-placed route. Four points from three games could put them in the mix for one of the eight best third-placed berths, though that would likely require a positive result against Colombia or DR Congo and avoiding a heavy defeat to Portugal.
[...]
1xBet offers odds of 1.87 for this country to pick up at least two points in the competition. Not only that, it offers 2.10 odds on Uzbekistan finishing in the top three in Group K.
